summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, and chronic abdominal pain was admitted with worsening epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. She reported the symptoms began after an iron infusion and felt different from her usual gastroparesis flares. She had recently completed a course of cefpodoxime for a urinary tract infection. Initial labs showed leukocytosis, hyperglycemia, and normocytic anemia. A stool test confirmed Clostridium difficile infection. She was treated with intravenous fluids and started on oral metronidazole for a 10-day course. Her symptoms improved, she tolerated oral intake, and her abdominal tenderness resolved. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete her antibiotic course and follow up with her primary care provider.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
